title: Frobenius-semilinear vector-bundle fixed points
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and $S$ a Noetherian scheme (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]) [def-pc-scheme] over $\mathbf F_p$. Let $E$ be an $\mathcal O_S$-module which Zariski-locally is isomorphic to $\mathcal O_S^{\oplus r}$ for some finite $r\geq0$, and view $E_{\mathrm{et}}$ as an abelian sheaf [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module] in the chosen coefficient universe. If sectionwise $\operatorname{ULift}$ is used, transport addition and scalar action along its bijection, and use the same lift for $\mathcal O_{S,\mathrm{et}}$. Let $F:E_{\mathrm{et}}\to E_{\mathrm{et}}$ be an additive sheaf morphism satisfying $F(ae)=a^pF(e)$ for every pair of local sections $a$ of $\mathcal O_{S,\mathrm{et}}$ and $e$ of $E_{\mathrm{et}}$. With kernel and cokernel in abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves],
$$\operatorname{Coker}(F-1)=0,\qquad\operatorname{Ker}(F-1)\text{ is constructible}$$
in the finite abelian stratum sense of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-abelian-sheaf]. Neither invertibility of $F$ nor constant rank on all of $S$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GKU, label lemma-frobenius-linear-on-vb; Noetherian specialization of both conclusions

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover $S=\bigcup_a W_a$ trivializing $E$, with $W_a=\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ and rank $n_a$. Such a cover exists by the given local trivializations, the affine-open basis and quasi-compactness. The locally Noetherian hypothesis implies that $S$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], so the global refinement lemma will apply in step 7. Work on one chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$, writing its basis as $e_1,\ldots,e_n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], restriction to this open agrees with abelian inverse image. By [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module] and [def-pc-module-pullback], on any etale $T\to W$ the pulled-back free module has basis $e_i$ and its sections are tuples in $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)^n$: tensoring a finite free module sends its basis to that of the free target-ring module. Write $F(e_j)=\sum_i c_{ij}e_i$, $c_{ij}\in A$. Additivity, semilinearity and naturality then give $(F-1)(\sum_j x_je_j)=\sum_i(\sum_j c_{ij}x_j^p-x_i)e_i$ on every such $T$.

source.place: Tag 0GKU, proof, affine trivialization and matrix formula

proof.text: For an affine etale $T=\operatorname{Spec}R\to W$ and target section $b=\sum_i b_ie_i$, define $B_b=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(b_i+x_i-\sum_j c_{ij}x_j^p)_{i=1}^n$, with the coefficients mapped from $A$ to $R$, and $Q_b=\operatorname{Spec}B_b$. Each partial derivative of $x_j^p$ is zero because $p=0$ in $R$, so the Jacobian of these $n$ equations in $n$ variables is the identity matrix. Its determinant is $1$, including when $n=0$. Thus this is a square Jacobian presentation [def-exc-jacobian-presentation], and [lem-exc-etale-jacobian-presentation] makes $R\to B_b$ etale of finite presentation. By the affine description of [def-weil-etale-morphism], $Q_b\to T$ is etale. The images of the variables satisfy $\sum_j c_{ij}x_j^p-x_i=b_i$, so their tuple is a preimage of $b$ on $Q_b$.

source.place: Tag 0GKU, proof of surjectivity, polynomial presentation and differential calculation; square-Jacobian criterion 00T6, 00T7, 00U9

proof.text: For every point $t\in T$ choose an algebraic closure $k$ of its residue field. The matrix $(c_{ij}(t))$ defines the additive $p$-linear map $k^n\to k^n$, $x\mapsto(\sum_j c_{ij}(t)x_j^p)_i$, since $(x+y)^p=x^p+y^p$. Its field has characteristic $p$, and its vector space has finite dimension $n$. Apply [lem-sc-lang-steinberg] to solve $(F_t-1)x=b(t)$. Sending the variables of $B_b$ to these coordinates gives a ring map $B_b\to k$ over $R$, hence a point of $Q_b$ above $t$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Thus $Q_b\to T$ is surjective, so it is a one-member etale covering by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For a general etale object and target section, first take an affine open cover and refine by the inverse images of the trivializing charts, then take these polynomial covers on affine refinements. This proves local surjectivity on every site object. By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective], $F-1$ is an epimorphism of abelian sheaves; its cokernel is zero in the abelian category. No faithful-flatness claim is needed beyond this etale covering. A sectionwise universe lift carries this calculation to the lifted sheaves by $x\mapsto\operatorname{ULift.up}(x)$ and its inverse, preserving the transported addition, scalar action and the displayed equations.

source.place: Tag 0GKU, proof, nonempty geometric fibres and local preimage; Tag 0A3L, lemma-F-1

proof.text: On the chart $W$ put $P=\operatorname{Spec}(A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(x_i-\sum_j c_{ij}x_j^p)_i)$. Step 2 with $b=0$ shows $P\to W$ is etale, and $P$ and $W$ are affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The sectionwise subgroup of sections killed by $F-1$ is itself a sheaf: glue its sections in $E$, and their image under $F-1$ is zero since it is zero on the cover. Every sheaf morphism killed by $F-1$ factors uniquely through this subgroup, so it is the categorical kernel by [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. For affine etale $T=\operatorname{Spec}R\to W$, an $A$-algebra map from the displayed quotient to $R$ is exactly a tuple solving $\sum_j c_{ij}x_j^p-x_i=0$. By step 1 that tuple is exactly a section of $K:=\operatorname{Ker}(F-1)$ over $T$. This correspondence commutes with restriction because it sends each variable to its coordinate. It extends to every etale $T$ by an affine open cover: coordinate tuples glue as sections, and the resulting morphisms to $P$ glue as scheme morphisms, uniquely on overlaps. Therefore the underlying sheaf of sets of $K|_W$ is the section sheaf $h_P$. The identification is valid in the chosen universe by lifting each coordinate tuple and each morphism along the same sectionwise bijection. This proves representability directly, rather than assuming that abelian inverse image of $E_{\mathrm{et}}$ equals the quasi-coherent module on an arbitrary closed stratum.

source.place: Tag 0GKU, proof of constructibility, displayed representing affine scheme

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-stratified-finite] to $P\to W$: both schemes are affine and the map is etale by step 4, so all its quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness hypotheses hold. Obtain a finite constructible locally closed immersed stratification $W=\coprod_b Z_b$ with $P_b:=P\times_W Z_b\to Z_b$ finite etale. For the stratum immersion $i_b:Z_b\to W$, [lem-galois-inverse-image-representable] gives $i_b^{-1}h_P\cong h_{P_b}$, since $P\to W$ is an object of $W_{\mathrm{et}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures], the underlying set sheaf of the abelian inverse image $i_b^{-1}(K|_W)$ is exactly this inverse image of its underlying set sheaf. Hence it is $h_{P_b}$. This uses represented sheaf pullback; it does not identify quasi-coherent sections before and after a closed base change.

source.place: Tag 0GKU, final paragraph, expanded via Tag 03S8 proof, Tag 03S0 and Tag 03Q1(4)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-yoneda-local-trivializations], $h_{P_b}$ is locally constant with finite geometric stalks. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-abelian-forget] to the abelian sheaf $i_b^{-1}(K|_W)$: it becomes locally constant as an abelian sheaf and its stalks are finite sets. On a nonempty member of a constant trivializing cover, its constant abelian group is isomorphic to the stalk at any algebraically closed geometric point, and so is finite; empty members can be dropped. Thus this is finite local constancy in precisely the abelian sense of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-abelian-sheaf], not merely finite generation of an abelian group. Repeat steps 4--6 on each of the finitely many charts $W_a$.

source.place: Tag 0GKU, final sentence, Tag 03S8(1) expanded using 03RV and the abelian clauses of 03RU

proof.text: The finite affine cover of step 1 and the finite chart stratifications of step 5 satisfy [lem-weil-pbc-etale-stratification-local-gluing-core]: $S$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis and quasi-separated by step 1. Choose its single finite constructible locally closed immersed stratification. For each stratum immersion $j:H\to S$, that lemma gives actual scheme morphisms $g:H\to Z_{a,b}$ and $f:Z_{a,b}\to W_a\to S$ with $j=f\circ g$. By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], $G:=f^{-1}K$ is the finite locally constant abelian sheaf obtained in step 6, and $j^{-1}K\cong g^{-1}G$.

source.place: Tag 0GKU, lemma-frobenius-linear-on-vb, affine locality reduction and final constructibility; expanded using Etale Cohomology Tags 03S0 and 095A

proof.text:
Choose the trivializing etale cover $v_i:V_i\to Z_{a,b}$ of $G$ from step 6, with finite abelian values $A_i$ and $G|_{V_i}\cong\underline{A_i}_{V_i}$; since each $v_i$ is etale, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] identifies this restriction with the abelian inverse image, so $v_i^{-1}G\cong\underline{A_i}_{V_i}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change], the projections $k_i:U_i:=H\times_{Z_{a,b}}V_i\to H$ form an etale covering. Write $q_i:U_i\to V_i$ for the other projection. The fibre-product identity $g\circ k_i=v_i\circ q_i$ and [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] give
$$k_i^{-1}g^{-1}G\cong q_i^{-1}v_i^{-1}G\cong q_i^{-1}\underline{A_i}_{V_i}.$$
Here composition is applied to morphisms of schemes, so neither projection $q_i$ nor $g$ is assumed etale.

source.place: Tag 0GKU, lemma-frobenius-linear-on-vb, affine locality reduction and final constructibility; expanded using Etale Cohomology Tags 03S0 and 095A

proof.text:
Apply [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant] to the scheme morphism $q_i$, with values in abelian groups and $M=A_i$. Its constant sheaves are those of [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], the sheafifications of the constant abelian presheaf with value $A_i$, and its pullback is the abelian inverse image, so it gives an isomorphism of abelian sheaves
$$q_i^{-1}\underline{A_i}_{V_i}\cong\underline{A_i}_{U_i}.$$
No etaleness, torsion or finiteness hypothesis on $q_i$ or $A_i$ is needed. This comparison preserves the value $A_i$ itself, so the values remain finite groups. Combined with step 8 and $j^{-1}K\cong g^{-1}G$, it trivializes $j^{-1}K$ on the covering $\{U_i\to H\}$.

source.place: Tag 0GKU, lemma-frobenius-linear-on-vb, affine locality reduction and final constructibility; expanded using Etale Cohomology Tags 03S0 and 095A

proof.text: Each stratum of the single global finite constructible partition of step 7 now has finite locally constant abelian inverse image, by steps 8--9. Apply [def-weil-pbc-constructible-abelian-sheaf] to this partition to conclude that $K$ is constructible. If $S$ is empty take the empty partition. For a rank zero chart the polynomial quotient is $R$, the solution cover is the identity and the kernel is the zero abelian sheaf. Together with step 3 this proves both conclusions, without any invertibility or globally constant-rank hypothesis on $F$.
